ROOT_CAUSE_row5_sampleA.verdict: FUNCTIONAL FAIL (not safety, not a HALT). Root cause has MOVED AGAIN, from L411 (now guarded) to L425-426.
ROOT_CAUSE_row5_sampleA.mechanism: L411 guard NOW SKIPS the decline-clobber (message_type==='request_for_help' -> condition false), so message_type survives past L414 as 'request_for_help'. BUT L425 `if (output.output.domain_hint) { output.output.message_type = 'business_query' }` — the LLM emitted domain_hint as the STRING "null" (truthy) -> L426 sets message_type='business_query'. Then L452 `_reqHelp = message_type === 'request_for_help'` reads 'business_query' -> _reqHelp=FALSE -> Tier-1 retarget guard L507 (`_reqHelp && _llmTeamN && _llmTeamN !== _priorTeam`) cannot fire even though _llmTeamN='warehouse' != _priorTeam='customer_service'. Falls through: _hasPickSignal true (is_affirmative===false), _pos/_pm empty -> L549 is_affirmative===false arm -> L554 escalation_declined + L555 message_type='casual'.
ROOT_CAUSE_row5_sampleA.why_nondeterministic: Samples B and C: the fork LLM emitted domain_hint as REAL JSON null -> L425 falsy -> message_type stays 'request_for_help' -> L452 _reqHelp=true -> L507 Tier-1 RETARGET FIRES correctly (routing->warehouse, escalation={is_escalation_confirmation:true, retarget_team:true}, selection_context null, last_result_set [], member_pick_context false) -> If2 TRUE -> human-intervention team=warehouse (guarded). The only differentiator across the 3 samples is the LLM's domain_hint value (string "null" vs real null).
ROOT_CAUSE_row5_sampleA.recommended_fix: output_exchange L425: coerce/guard the string 'null' (and 'undefined') — e.g. `const _dh = (output.output.domain_hint && output.output.domain_hint !== 'null' && output.output.domain_hint !== 'undefined') ? output.output.domain_hint : null; output.output.domain_hint = _dh; if (_dh) { output.output.message_type = 'business_query'; }`. OR normalize the LLM output earlier so domain_hint 'null'-string -> null globally (safer: several downstream truthy checks key on domain_hint). NOTE: the systemMessage should also be tightened to emit real null, but code robustness (string-'null' coercion) is the reliable fix since LLM output is variable. A live promotion of the parser change must ship BOTH the systemMessage AND this output_exchange fix (in addition to the L411 guard already applied).
